notes: Do not source weapon/item tiles from guessed common_chr offsets.
NES tile IDs >= 0x70 are valid only when backed by live CHR bytes.

item_defs.name: sword_vert
item_defs.sprite_size_override_reason: NES uses 8x16 hardware sprites (PPU OAM obj size bit): tile $20 is the top 8x8, tile $21 is the bottom 8x8 of the same 8x16 sprite. Anim_WriteSpecificItemSprites @Narrow (Z_01.asm:5288) emits a single OAM entry whose hardware height is 16px. Genesis SPRITE_SIZE(1,2) matches NES visual output exactly. The dispatch table [1,1] reflects the NES tile-count per OAM entry, not the rendered pixel height.

item_defs.name: sword_horz
item_defs.sprite_size_override_reason: NES Flippable dispatch (Z_01.asm:5301) draws two 8x8 sprites side-by-side (tiles $82+$84, 16x8 visible). Genesis renderer stores all 4 tiles ($82-$85, the full 2x2 NES CHR block) in a 2x2 SPRITE_SIZE so both the top row and bottom row are uploaded and accessible for Genesis column-major tile layout. SPRITE_SIZE(2,1) would omit bottom-row tiles needed for the sword cross-guard graphic.

item_defs.name: boomerang
item_defs.nes_dispatch_note: NES PPU 8x16 mode: each OAM entry tile $36/$38/$3A/$3C pairs with $37/$39/$3B/$3D as bottom half. Live BizHawk capture (probe_nes_throw.lua frame 280) confirmed: tile $36 has only rows 4-7 of curve; tile $37 has only rows 0-3 — combined 8x16 = full L-shape boomerang. Atlas idx 6/7, 8/9, 10/11, 12/13 are adjacent in items_chr_x4.
item_defs.sprite_size_override_reason: NES PPU runs in 8x16 sprite mode (PPUCTRL bit 5 = 1) during gameplay. verify_item_chr_manifest classify_nes_dispatch reads 'Narrow' as 8x8 (sprite_size [1,1]) but @Narrow refers to half-WIDTH not 8x8 height. Live BizHawk capture (probe_nes_throw.lua frame 280) shows OAM 'tile $X' renders both $X (top 8x8) + $X+1 (bottom 8x8) as one 8x16 sprite. Renderer must use SPRITE_SIZE(1,2). See Anim_WriteSpecificItemSprites @Narrow Z_01.asm:5288 + PPUCTRL setup.

Anim_WriteSpecificItemSprites @Narrow (Z_01.asm:5288) emits a single 8x16 OAM entry. Genesis SPRITE_SIZE(1,2) matches NES rendered height. Same reasoning as sword_vert.

item_defs.name: explosion
item_defs.nes_dispatch_note: DrawOtherBombClouds (Z_07.asm:4936) draws cloud cluster via DrawBombOrCloudNoFlashing -> Anim_WriteItemSprites with item slot $01, frames 1-3 -> ItemFrameTiles[$04..$06] = $70/$72/$74. Each tile in [$6C,$7C) -> @Wide -> Anim_WriteMirroredSpritePair (Z_01.asm:5304): 2 8x8 sprites side-by-side, right=left hflipped, total 16x8. Generator emits 2 Genesis tiles per NES tile (raw + hflipped) so SGDK SPRITE_SIZE(2,1) renders both halves.
item_defs.sprite_size_override_reason: NES @Wide_Mirrored writes 2 OAMs side-by-side. PPU 8x16 sprite mode (PPUCTRL bit 5 = 1) makes each OAM 8x16 (paired tiles), so visible explosion frame = 2*8x16 = 16x16. Live BizHawk capture (probe_nes_explode.lua frame 335) confirms 4 cluster positions × 2 OAMs each (hfl=0 left + hfl=1 right) for tile $70/$72/$74. Each tile pairs with $71/$73/$75 as bottom half. Genesis renderer needs SPRITE_SIZE(2,2) per cluster.

item_defs.name: sword_diag
item_defs.sprite_size_override_reason: Genesis-native ALttP-style diagonal sword swing (Redux mode). NES Z1 has no diagonal sword sprite; the diagonal swing is a Genesis extension with no NES dispatch equivalent. Tiles $48-$4B form the full 2x2 diagonal blade graphic. NES dispatch classification of nes_frame_tile $48 as Narrow is inapplicable here.

item_defs.name: candle_fire_f0
item_defs.nes_dispatch_note: UpdateFire (Z_07.asm:4622) draws fire via DrawObjectWithType anim index $40 (uses $41 after INY) -> ObjAnimations[$41]=$08 -> ObjAnimFrameHeap[$08+frame] tile pairs ($5C/$5E, $9E/$A0, $44/$46, $CE/$D0). Each frame is 2 NES tiles side-by-side (left+2=right per DrawObjectWithAnimAndSpecificSprites). ObjAnimAttrHeap[$08+frame] sub_pal sequence = (2, 0, 0, 1). Animation: 4 frames @ 4 ticks each (LDA #$04 / Anim_AdvanceAnimCounter).
item_defs.sprite_size_override_reason: NES PPU runs 8x16 sprite mode (PPUCTRL bit 5 = 1). @Wide_Slim draws 2 OAMs side-by-side, each 8x16 (paired tile $X+1 as bottom). Visible cluster = 2*8x16 = 16x16, NOT 16x8. Renderer uses SPRITE_SIZE(2,2) with column-major fetch order LT, LB, RT, RB. Live BizHawk capture in probe_nes_audit.lua confirmed bottom-half tile bytes for $5D/$5F/$9F/$A1/$45/$47/$CF/$D1/$7B/$7D/$7F/$6F/$71.

DrawFairy (Z_04.asm:11508) toggles frame every 4 video frames (ASL / AND FrameCounter / LSR LSR -> $0C). Both tiles in [$20,$62) -> @Narrow dispatch (single 8x16 sprite per OAM entry, NES PPU 8x16 obj-size mode). Anim_SetSpriteDescriptorRedPaletteRow forces sub-pal row 1 (red).
item_defs.sprite_size_override_reason: NES uses 8x16 hardware sprites (PPU OAM obj size bit). Tile $50 is the top 8x8, tile $51 is the bottom 8x8 of one 8x16 hardware sprite (and $52/$53 likewise for frame 1). Anim_WriteSpecificItemSprites @Narrow (Z_01.asm:5288) emits a single OAM entry whose hardware height is 16 px. Genesis SPRITE_SIZE(1,2) matches NES visual output exactly. Identical pattern to the existing sword_vert / arrow_vert manifest entries.
